request.description: Native pixel-art modular prop study for an enchanted woodland shrine match-three game, 128x128 transparent sprite atlas. EXACTLY FOUR SEPARATE compact natural assets in four 56x56 quadrants with generous clear space between them, not a complete scene or UI frame. TOP LEFT: low moss-covered chunky blue-gray stone with two small warm russet woodland mushrooms at its foot, broad caps and cream stems, 3 sparse cream cap spots, simple olive leaves. TOP RIGHT: mossy curved dark brown tree ROOT rising vertically then curling left, slim upright hook shape, two leafy offshoots, no giant tree. BOTTOM LEFT: a small curving BRANCH TIP with 4-5 large pointed olive leaves, unified connected silhouette, narrow vertical arrangement. BOTTOM RIGHT: low irregular MOSSY STONE and a separate connected tuft of 4 broad pointed fern leaves, one tiny amber mushroom. Each object has complete outlines and 3 transparent pixels around silhouette. Natural purposeful groups, premium calm woodland, chunky dark contour, broad connected planes, top-left lighting with 2-3 tones per material, no dithering, no gradients, no blur, no AA. Root wood subdued warm brown, leaf ramps dark olive/soft muted yellow green, stone cool desaturated slate, mushrooms warm muted rust/amber and cream, all compatible with provided reference. The objects decorate the narrow outer side margins and foot corners of a game board. No gems, skulls, faces, creatures, jewels, text, rectangular frames, ground platform or background. Follow Rattlebones reference only for crisp outline, cluster economy and rendering discipline, not anatomy or royal colors.

reference_images.usage: The side roots, mossy rocks, pointed foliage and mushrooms outside the board and lower HUD establish the woodland materials and ornamental identity. Generate only four isolated modular props in a 2x2 atlas, no scene, UI or character.
